what: Independent replication of the declaration experiment's non-identical results.
why: A single run of a live-internet measurement is a point estimate. Every target whose two User-Agents produced different content was re-probed by a separate run of the same harness, on a different process, minutes later. A finding that does not come back is not a finding.
method: Same 4-pass interleaved design (generic, declared, generic, declared), same visible-text comparison.

replicated.name: Discourse (meta)
replicated.detail: declared UA received 781 characters of visible text; the browser UA received 325,272. Reproduced in both runs.

replicated.name: X
replicated.detail: declared UA received 26 characters of visible text; the browser UA received 173, plus a redirect the declared UA did not get. Reproduced in both runs.

replicated.name: Google
replicated.detail: declared UA received 230 characters of visible text; the browser UA received 3,217. Reproduced in both runs.

replicated.name: Product Hunt
replicated.detail: The inversion is real and reproducible: the declared agent UA received the full page (365,178 characters) while the browser UA received a 16-character stub with HTTP 403.

replicated.name: New York Times
replicated.detail: Scored as a consistent, reproducible 65% visible-text overlap in run 3, but the replication run's own browser-UA control failed to reproduce itself, so the target is unstable and the difference cannot be attributed to the User-Agent. Reported as unresolved, not as a finding.

unchanged_expectation: The 24 identical results were not re-probed individually; the replication targets the claims, not the null results.
interpretation_guard: The User-Agent line is changed as a whole string, so a difference is attributable to the whole string, not specifically to declaring non-humanness. A site that downgrades an unknown non-Mozilla client may be reacting to unfamiliarity rather than to the self-identification.
